subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers — Nova Retail
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLOs & cost levers — Nova Retail

Hi Evan (and Jade),

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation with the Nova product team. Per our call, I wanted to capture the performance targets and propose the immediate levers we can use to hit the SLOs while keeping monthly inference costs predictable. Please review and confirm assumptions so we can scope a short PoC.

Recap of SLOs you called out
- P95 generation latency target: <= 200 ms for 256-token responses (interactive discovery flows)
- Sustained throughput: ~3,000 generated responses/hour (~50rps peak bursts)
- Concurrent user sessions identified for launch: 40–60 concurrent streams (50 nominal)
- Streaming requirement: progressive token streaming for UX (first token <100 ms ideally)

Key assumptions I used for cost/feasibility questions (please correct):
- Average prompt length: ~60 tokens; average response: 220–260 tokens
- Percent of sessions needing streaming: ~80% (rest are batch/async)
- Quality: must match current vendor baseline for instruction-following — prefer model family similar to Llama 2 / open weights if possible

Immediate cost/perf levers to try (short list we can implement for PoC)
1) Continuous batching + smart routing
   - Use Redwood's continuous batching to increase GPU utilization while preserving P95 by routing low-latency traffic to dedicated low-latency nodes and background traffic to pooled nodes.
2) KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts
   - Cache common prefixes (search/context vectors) to shave ~15–30% off token compute for discovery flows that reuse templates.
3) Quantization profiles + mixed precision
   - For non-critical high-throughput paths, use 4-bit quantization profile A (recommended) for ~2.5–3x cost savings with small quality delta. Reserve FP16 runs for high-quality narrow flows.
4) Model variants and fallbacks
   - Default to a quantized LLaMA-family variant for standard conversations; fallback to a higher-precision variant only on flagged sessions (A/B controlable).
5) Streaming optimization
   - Enable early-token micro-batching and prioritized kernel selection to meet first-token <100ms.

Next steps I propose
- You: confirm prompt/response token averages and % streaming sessions (Jade if you can attach traffic sample that'd be great).
- Us: run a quick cost model and capacity sketch (we'll include expected token cost delta for each quantization profile + projected P95 latency).
- Schedule a 30-min technical PoC kickoff next week to validate with a small traffic replay (we can run on Dedicated or Hosted with a private VPC).

Attaching: a short SLA/PoC outline PDF I'll circulate (see attachments) — will convert to a short mutual action plan once we have the traffic sample.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick engineering notes that may help scope the PoC:
- If average response length is >200 tokens, we'll want to test both the quantized 4-bit profile and a 16-bit fallback.
- For KV caching: we can instrument prefix hit-rate; if hit-rate >25% we likely see >20% cost reduction for discovery flows.
- Batching: continuous batching reduces unit cost but can increase tail latency; we'll run an SLO-aware batching policy that enforces max batch wait <10ms for low-latency lane.
